span.term: An inverted-U relation between dopamine transmission and inhibitory processing: amphetamine pushes low-NP animals toward and high-NP animals past an optimum, so the same drug raises or abolishes priming depending on baseline state

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Brief primes are routed through preconscious, automatic processing, which is the route that generates negative priming; longer primes recruit more controlled processing and weaken it
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A species difference in speed-accuracy strategy - rats protect response speed and sacrifice accuracy - channels the priming cost into accuracy rather than latency

span.label: NEGATIVE PRIMING - a priming effect defined as a LOSS, and defined as the NORMAL one: `Quotation withheld` Second record tonight whose priming effect harms performance (after Keane2015's costs), and the first where the harm is the healthy result
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: LESS PRIMING IS THE DEFICIT - the direction that inverts everything. `TS subjects exhibit DIMINISHED NP`, so a smaller effect is the pathological finding and a larger one is intact function. Any summary that treats priming magnitude as one quantity with a good direction gets this record backwards, and the corpus contains many records where more priming is the notable result
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: PRIMING AS A PROGNOSTIC INDEX - `their NP levels PREDICT THEIR RESPONSE TO BEHAVIORAL THERAPY`. Not a phenomenon under study, not an instrument for probing representations, but a clinical measurement used to forecast treatment outcome. A fourth job for the word in this corpus, alongside phenomenon, instrument and paradigm
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: THE EFFECT ONLY APPEARS UNDER CHALLENGE, which is a fact about the animal model rather than about the animals: `during the SHORT PRIME CHALLENGE, rats exhibited lower accuracy in NP vs. baseline trials`. A 0.25 s prime was needed to make the phenomenon measurable at all, and the same duration was then carried into the drug study. A translational model whose sensitivity had to be engineered into the timing
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: negative priming —operationalised-as→ inhibitory information processing
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — The measurement claim the whole paper rests on: a deficit in inhibitory processing `can be detected using a negative priming task`, so the loss of performance is read as the mechanism working. Direction matters - the effect is the INDEX and the inhibitory process is what it indexes, not the other way round.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Tourette syndrome —causes→ negative priming
span.note: direction on the measure: reduces · strength of the relation: 0.9 — `reduces` is correct and reads backwards without the sense rows: the reduction is a reduction OF A REDUCTION. Negative priming is itself a performance loss, and Tourette patients show LESS of it - so less priming is the pathological direction here.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: prime duration —causes→ negative priming
span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.85 — Shortening the prime makes the effect bigger, which is why 0.25 s was carried into the drug study. Weighted 0.85: the sentence reports the choice retrospectively as a reason for a design decision rather than presenting the duration comparison as a result.

span.label: Rats trained on the new task showed a robust negative priming effect, performing worse when the target appeared where the distractor had just been.

span.label: The authors report this as the first rodent paradigm measuring visuospatial priming.

span.label: Shortening the prime from 0.5 s to 0.25 s strengthened the negative priming effect.

span.label: Lengthening the prime from 0.5 s to 1 s weakened negative priming, the mirror image of the short-prime result.

span.label: Each animal's degree of negative priming was consistent across two repetitions of the short-prime challenge, suggesting NP is a stable individual trait.

span.label: Amphetamine abolished negative priming at every dose in rats that showed strong drug-free priming.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: In rats the negative priming effect appeared in accuracy rather than in response latency, unlike the human task where latency is the more robust index.

span.label: Amphetamine reliably increased premature responding at all doses, while leaving trials completed unaffected.
